title: Compatible root bases compare the finite towers on the prescribed slice
statement: Use [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], and [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Fix a prime ell invertible in every residue field of a scheme X and a pro-etale object W. For every n>=0 let zeta_n be a section of mu_(ell^(n+1)) on W and let e_n be an isomorphism from the restricted constant Z/ell^(n+1) module unit to that root module. Assume the root power transition sends zeta_(n+1) to zeta_n and e_n sends every scalar on every V->W to its product with the restriction of zeta_n. For each finite intermediate coefficient field E, reconstruct section modules by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and retain the integral O_E,X action. The actual finite integral twist tower [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] is naturally isomorphic on W to the ell-power quotient coefficient tower constructed for [lem-sp-ell-coefficient-cone-limit]. This asserts only an isomorphism of finite-level diagrams, with their specified reductions and root power transitions, and no inverse-limit or rational basis.

proof.text: At each positive exponent, apply lem-sp-root-basis-level to the supplied single root section, basis isomorphism and normalization. Choose its coefficient-to-twist isomorphism i_n with the specified formula on every slice object. This theorem is only a single-level calculation: it has neither adjacent levels nor transition hypotheses.

proof.text: For every slice object V -> W, naturality of the actual root transition identifies transition(zeta_(n+1)|V) with transition(zeta_(n+1))|V. The supplied h_zeta identifies the latter with zeta_n|V. Thus the root generator transition equation holds on every slice object, not just W.

proof.text: The actual integral transition has underlying sheaf map equal to the tensor of coefficient reduction and root transition, by spIntegralLevelTransition_existsUnique. Evaluate lax monoidal tensor naturality at b tensor zeta_(n+1)|V, and use the preceding root identity and the normalized i_n formulas. This proves coefficientReduction followed by i_n equals i_(n+1) followed by twistTransition as morphisms of the reconstructed integral module sheaves. NatTrans.ofOpSequence extends these successor squares to all arrows. Every component is an isomorphism, so NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app makes the natural transformation invertible; invert it for the requested twist-to-coefficient orientation.

theorem spRootBasisTowerComparison
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (ℓ : X.residueField x)] (W : X.ProEt)
    (ζ : ∀ n : ℕ, (Scheme.purTwistRootsModule X ℓ n).val.obj (op W))
    (e : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Scheme.purTwistRing X (Scheme.purTwistFiniteRing X ℓ n))).over W ≅
        (Scheme.purTwistRootsModule X ℓ n).over W)
    (hζ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (Scheme.proEtaleRootsOfUnityTransition X (ℓ ^ (n + 1)) (ℓ ^ (n + 2))
        (pow_pos (Fact.out : ℓ.Prime).pos _) (pow_pos (Fact.out : ℓ.Prime).pos _)
        (pow_dvd_pow ℓ (Nat.le_succ (n + 1)))).hom.app (op W) (ζ (n + 1)) = ζ n)
    (he : ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : (Over W)ᵒᵖ)
      (a : ((Scheme.purTwistRing X (Scheme.purTwistFiniteRing X ℓ n)).over W).obj.obj V),
      (e n).hom.val.app V a =
        a • (Scheme.purTwistRootsModule X ℓ n).val.map V.unop.hom.op (ζ n))
    (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ) :
    Nonempty (spIntegralTwistSystem X ℓ E ⋙ spRootBasisSliceSections X
        (condensedRingObj.{u} (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} ℓ E.1) X) W ≅
      spEllCoefficientSystem X ℓ E ⋙ spRootBasisSliceSections X
        (condensedRingObj.{u} (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} ℓ E.1) X) W)
